title: Lyon 2021 §6 T-junction extension: arc-splitting case (no matching node)
description: PATCH-77 v1 handles the case where the T-junction's mirror parametric distance hits an existing node on the opposite side. When it falls mid-arc, the arc must be split: introduce a new TNode at that distance, slice the existing TArc into two DERIVED LayoutArcs (covering [0,t] and [t,1]), then fall through to the matching-node case. The DERIVED LayoutArc variant is already defined; what's missing is (a) the arc-split logic in QuadLayoutExtractor, (b) the per-arc sub-quantization split (q[a] = q_left + q_right), and (c) inserting the new layout node into the layout's node list. On rocker-arm with real ILP q from PATCH-76, this is the gating fix to bring #P from 13 toward metriko's 96 / Lyon's 159.
definition-of-done: QuadLayoutExtractor handles the arc-splitting case; rocker-arm benchmark shows skipped count drops from 10 toward 0; Hand-30k drops from 15 toward 0. Tests: extend LayoutArcTest with an arc-splitting fixture (q values that force a mid-arc match).
testing-plan: Toy: 1-T-junction patch with q causing mid-arc match → patch splits via DERIVED arcs into 2 conforming patches. Hand-30k & rocker-arm regressions: report tJunctionsResolved + skipped.
